bullets.title: Fed's Waller puts July rate hike back on the table if CPI surprises hot
bullets.body: Governor Waller said another hot core inflation print this week could force policymakers to consider raising rates 'in the near term,' marking the clearest hawkish signal from a Fed official this cycle. He cited tariffs, energy prices, and AI buildout demand as upward inflation drivers, said past increases can no longer be blamed on tariffs alone, and requires 'a couple more' downside readings to confirm progress. Markets repriced quickly: fed funds futures moved from 35% to ~50% odds of a July hike.

bullets.title: Waller: inflation target range of 1.5–2.5% preferred over fixed 2%; no symbolic hikes
bullets.body: Waller expressed personal preference for a 1.5%–2.5% inflation target band versus a single 2% point, said he is 'not interested in symbolic rate hikes,' and emphasized maximum transparency—arguing no economic theory supports withholding information from markets. He sees no issues with the balance sheet at current size and no need for scarce reserves policy.

bullets.title: Treasuries fall, gold drops 3%, yields surge on Waller hawkishness and oil spike
bullets.body: US 10-year yields hit 4.60%, UK 10-year approached 5.0%, and German 10-year sat at 3.10% as markets reacted to Waller's comments and surging oil prices. Spot gold fell 3%+ to ~$3,994/oz—down over 20% from its January record high of $5,318—as safe-haven bids reversed on the rate-hike repricing.

bullets.title: Oil surges 7%+ above $76/bbl: Iran blockade, Houthi attacks, Hormuz near-closure
bullets.body: WTI rose 7.3% above $76/bbl (Brent near $80) after Trump reinstated the Iranian naval blockade, Houthi forces launched multiple ballistic missile waves at Saudi airports, and Strait of Hormuz commercial transits collapsed to just 3 crossings. Polymarket traders now betting crude oil exceeds $80 this month. The blockade has a 24-hour legal notification requirement before formal enforcement begins.

bullets.title: Trump claims 'Guardian of Hormuz': 20% cargo levy proposed, naval blockade of Iran reinstated
bullets.body: Trump posted on Truth Social reinstating the Iranian blockade and proposing a 20% reimbursement fee on all non-Iranian cargo transiting the Strait, positioning the U.S. as 'Guardian of the Hormuz Strait.' Iran's Revolutionary Guards rejected the move and asserted continued control; the UN shipping agency said no legal basis exists for mandatory strait tolls. Dubai/UAE responded by accelerating plans for an east-coast port bypass.

bullets.title: Strait of Hormuz effectively closed: 52% week-on-week traffic decline
bullets.body: Confirmed crossings fell ~52% week-on-week (July 10–12), with vessels shifting to Iranian and dark routes and IMO/Omani corridor activity dropping to minimal levels. Commercial transits hit as low as 3 crossings in a session (~1 tanker), with less than 50% probability of traffic normalization in 2026.

bullets.title: SPY: $1.7–2B put wall at 750 being tested; A/D line at all-time highs
bullets.body: SPY is testing a $2B put wall at the 750 level—bulls must hold or risk further downside—while separately the SPY advance/decline line has been hitting all-time highs, suggesting broad-based participation beneath the surface despite the geopolitical-driven volatility.

bullets.title: Mag 7 mixed at open: NVDA –1.2%, META –0.8% lead decliners; MSFT/GOOGL/AMZN +0.3%
bullets.body: Premarket saw Nvidia down 1.2% and Meta down 0.8% as chip stocks tumbled on Iran/Korea contagion, while Microsoft, Alphabet, and Amazon each gained 0.3% and Apple added 0.2%. Tesla fell 0.6%.

bullets.title: Korea margin call contagion: 1.2M accounts hit, Kospi 3rd-worst day since Lehman
bullets.body: As of July 13, 1.2 million Korean leveraged retail accounts triggered margin calls with 320k–360k fully liquidated; retail brokerage deposits fell 30 trillion won to the lowest since February 2020. The KORU 3x Kospi ETF is down 65% from its June 1 all-time high, erasing all 2024 gains. SK Hynix ADR fell 9.9% to session lows despite its US offering being 7x oversubscribed—the drop attributed to profit-taking and Korean/ADR repricing, not AI demand weakness.

bullets.title: Morgan Stanley raises hyperscaler capex forecasts: $1.2T in 2027, $1.4T in 2028
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley lifted its 2027 US hyperscaler capex estimate by 9% to $1.2 trillion and its 2028 estimate by 10% to $1.4 trillion, dismissing the narrative that a correction in AI infrastructure names signals the end of the buildout. Big Tech (Google, Amazon, Microsoft, Meta, Oracle) has already accumulated nearly $700B in debt to fund AI data centers.

bullets.title: TSMC reports 68% YoY June revenue surge; Q2 beats guidance at $40.2B
bullets.body: TSMC reported June net revenue of NT$442.68B ($13.79B), up 67.9% YoY and 6.2% MoM, with H1 2026 revenue of $74.99B (+35.6% YoY). Q2 revenue came in at $40.2B, above the high end of guidance. Options pricing a 3.57% implied move around the July 16 earnings print.

bullets.title: Memory supply tight until H2 2027; HBM demand crowding out commodity DRAM
bullets.body: Semianalysis analyst Ray Wang says memory supply is unlikely to improve until the second half of 2027, with DRAM remaining constrained as chipmakers balance HBM demand from AI against commodity RAM. HBM carries enormous opportunity cost versus commodity DRAM, where margins currently sit near 90%.

bullets.title: Buffett Indicator at record 234%—3 standard deviations above historical average
bullets.body: The US stock market value-to-GDP ratio hit a new record of 234%, more than 3 standard deviations above the long-term historical average, while S&P 500 earnings are expected to surge 24% this year—a level unprecedented outside post-recessionary rebounds, largely driven by big tech EPS. Analysts warn projecting recent extraordinary growth rates 5 years forward is a classic bubble signal.

bullets.title: Hedge funds hold near-record SOFR short; July hike probability jumps to 45–50%
bullets.body: Hedge funds are maintaining near-record short positions in SOFR futures. Following Waller's speech, short-term rate futures moved to price a 45–50% probability of a Fed rate hike at the July meeting, up from 35% earlier in the session.

bullets.title: Global central banks reducing USD exposure; yen weakens past ¥162/$
bullets.body: Reports indicate global central banks are reducing U.S. dollar reserve exposure. Separately, the yen has weakened above ¥162/USD as media reports suggested domestic Japanese pension funds face no pressure to buy more JGBs, adding upward pressure on global yields.

bullets.title: Meta announces $40B+ Louisiana data center; UBS cuts META target to $766 from $865
bullets.body: Meta announced capital expenditure exceeding $40 billion for a Louisiana data center development—adding to the hyperscaler AI buildout wave—while UBS simultaneously cut its META price target by ~11% to $766 from $865, signaling reduced near-term upside despite the capex commitment.

bullets.title: Intel commits $5.7B to Ireland Fab 34 for Xeon 6 and Diamond Rapids; Gelsinger buys $500K
bullets.body: Intel announced a €5B ($5.7B) investment at its Leixlip Ireland Fab 34 to scale Intel 3 production targeting Xeon 6 and next-gen Diamond Rapids processors. On the same day, former CEO Patrick Gelsinger purchased 153,846 shares for $500K as a director, part of a combined $6M insider buy across three executives—a notable coordinated signal.

bullets.title: Key macro week ahead: CPI/PPI, retail sales, Warsh testimony, TSMC earnings
bullets.body: The week features CPI (critical given Waller's hike threat), PPI, retail sales, Kevin Warsh Fed chair testimony, China data, and TSMC earnings (July 16, 1:30am ET, 3.57% implied move). Inflation data this week is the single most important input for the July FOMC rate decision.

bullets.title: AI bond issuance wave approaching $250B tests investor limits
bullets.body: A quarter-trillion-dollar wave of AI-related bond issuance is underway as hyperscalers and infrastructure companies race to fund data center buildouts, with investors' appetite being tested by the pace and volume of offerings.

bullets.title: September government shutdown risk: Trump threatens to withhold support without filibuster end
bullets.body: Trump warned of a potential government shutdown in September if the Senate does not eliminate the filibuster, adding a tail-risk policy event to an already congested macro calendar in Q3.
